<explanation>
Below is a detailed guideline tailored specifically for AiNiee, a sophisticated AI translation tool with a modular, multi-format, and multi-platform design. The system design diagram should reflect the complex interplay between file handling, AI platform interfacing, plugin extensions, and a flexible UI. Follow these steps to capture every essential element:

1. Project Overview & Main Components:
   • Identify the project type – AiNiee is a full-stack desktop (or GUI) tool primarily focused on AI-based translation for games, novels, subtitles, documents, etc. The README emphasizes multi-format support, integration with multiple LLM platforms, and a plug-in system.
   • Main architectural components include:
     - Core Engine and Base Modules: Represented by AiNiee.py and the “Base” folder (Base.py, EventManager.py, PluginManager.py). This layer coordinates events, plugin loading, and overall workflow.
     - File I/O and Conversion Layer: Under “ModuleFolders” are subfolders for FileReader, FileOutputer, FileConverter, FileAccessor—as well as Cache management. These components handle various file formats (JSON, DOCX, EPUB, TXT, etc.), performing reading, conversion, and saving operations.
     - API & Translation Services: Modules like “LLMRequester”, “Translator”, and “PromptBuilder” encapsulate the communication with external AI platforms as shown in the README and the LLMRequester submodules (OpenaiRequester, GoogleRequester, etc.). Also include RequestLimiter, ResponseChecker, and ResponseExtractor modules.
     - Widget & UI Components: The “DRWidget”, “UserInterface”, and “Widget” directories provide UI controls and configuration panels to set up translation projects, select APIs, change prompt settings, and manage UI interactions. They include settings pages, status monitoring, plugin management, and file operations.
     - Plugin Extensions: The “PluginScripts” folder contains various plugins (e.g., BilingualPlugin, LanguageFilter, TextNormalizer, etc.) that add extra functionalities. These plugins extend or modify the core translation workflow.
     - Supporting Resources: “Resource” holds localization files, prompt text files, regex definitions, and updater executables.

2. Relationships and Data Flow:
   • Begin by showing the user interaction at the top of the diagram—illustrate the GUI (UserInterface/DRSetting, Quality, Platform, Setting, etc.) where a user sets up the translation project (input/output folders, source/target languages, API selection, etc.).
   • Show an arrow from the UI to the Core Engine (AiNiee.py + Base modules) which acts as the orchestrator.
   • Next, detail the file flow:
     - The FileReader modules (ModuleFolders/FileReader) read original documents.
     - The FileConverter (ModuleFolders/FileConverter) can process files between formats as needed.
     - Then come the FileOutputers which write translated text to the designated output.
   • The translation workflow should branch to include the “Translator” component which, in turn, connects with LLMRequester and PromptBuilder modules to structure requests and communicate with external AI platforms.
   • Layer in the plugins: Display a plug-in layer that intercepts or modifies content through PluginManager from the “PluginScripts” folder, adding functionalities such as language filtering, text normalization, or specialized translation checks.
   • Also, illustrate the ancillary modules, such as RequestLimiter, ResponseExtractor, and ResponseChecker, that ensure proper throughput and quality control.

3. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles:
   • Emphasize modularity and separation of concerns:
     - UI is distinct from core translation logic.
     - All file operations are abstracted into dedicated modules.
     - External API interfacing is encapsulated in specialized modules.
     - Plugin-based extensibility allows one to add or update functionality without changing the core code.
   • Use directional arrows to represent data flow: Input data flows from file readers to the core engine, then out via API calls, then back to file writers, with plugins intercepting throughout.
   • Labels should clearly state each component (for example: “User Interface – Project Settings Page”, “Core Engine – Event Manager”, “FileReader – DocxReader”, “Plugin – TextNormalizer”, etc.).

4. Diagram Tailoring Graphical Elements:
   • Color-code or use distinct shapes:
     - Use one color/shape for UI components (e.g., rounded rectangles for UserInterface and Widget layers).
     - A different color for core modules (Base, AiNiee.py) and orchestration.
     - Another color for file I/O modules (ModuleFolders) and external API layers.
     - Highlight plugin components perhaps in a contrasting hue.
   • Clearly mark directional interactions (like arrows) that show, for example, translation inputs from UI → Core → Translator → External API and feedback loops for caching and error handling.
   • Include textual annotations for each major module:
     - Note multi-format support (indicate supported file types such as DOCX, EPUB, SRT, MD).
     - Mention multi-platform support for LLM connections (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, etc.).
     - Capture how the prompt builder and AI model configuration ties back to user settings in the UI.

5. Additional Considerations:
   • For a full-stack application like AiNiee:
     - Separate the front-end (UserInterface, Widget, DRWidget modules) from the business logic (Base, Translator, LLMRequester) and file-handling layers (ModuleFolders).
     - Ensure to represent the integration of plugins, showing how PluginManager dynamically loads functionality from the “PluginScripts” folder.
     - Represent integrations with external services (API platforms), showing configuration details as per the README’s “接口简介”.
   • Include icons or small diagrams illustrating connections with external resources (e.g., the gateway to OpenAI, Deepseek, etc.) to show the multi-LLM backend.

6. Practical Steps for Drawing the Diagram:
   1. Begin with a high-level block diagram capturing major layers: 
      - “User Interface Layer” with UI pages (Project Settings, Translation, Monitoring, etc.)
      - “Core Engine Layer” (AiNiee.py, Base, EventManager, PluginManager)
      - “File Handling Layer” (ModuleFolders: FileReader, FileOutputer, FileConverter)
      - “AI & Processing Layer” (Translator, LLMRequester, PromptBuilder, RequestLimiter, ResponseChecker)
      - “Plugin Extensibility Layer” (PluginScripts)
      - “Resource and Configuration” (Resource folder containing localization, regex, prompt files)
   2. Connect the layers with directional arrows to represent the data flow—from user-initiated project configuration to reading files, processing translation requests, utilizing plugins, and outputting results.
   3. Next, add annotations or sub-blocks to represent internal details where needed (for example, show different plugins and how they “hook” to the main flow).
   4. Finalize with clear labels, a legend for color-coding, and notes to highlight the multi-format, multi-platform translation emphasis.

By following these instructions, you can create a detailed and accurate system design diagram that maps out AiNiee’s comprehensive architecture. This diagram will serve as an excellent reference for development and troubleshooting, ensuring each component and its interactions are clearly understood.
</explanation>
